questions.q: In the TOGAF Standard, the term 'enterprise' is best described as which of the following?
o: A single legal company with shareholders
Any collection of organizations with a common set of goals
The IT department of a large corporation
questions.e: An enterprise is any collection of organizations that has a common set of goals; it may be a whole corporation, a division, a government agency, or a group of geographically distant organizations linked by common ownership.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Enterprise Architecture according to the TOGAF Standard?
o: To document the current IT estate
To guide effective and efficient change in pursuit of the enterprise's goals
questions.e: The purpose of EA is to guide effective, efficient, agile, and durable change in support of the organization's target outcomes.

questions.q: Which of the following lists the four architecture domains defined by the TOGAF Standard?
questions.e: The four architecture domains are Business, Data, Application, and Technology (Data and Application together form the Information Systems Architectures).

questions.q: What is the primary use of the Enterprise Continuum?
o: To classify and structure re-usable architecture and solution assets
To assign business value to work packages
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum is a view for classifying and structuring re-usable architecture and solution assets, ranging from generic Foundation Architectures to Organization-Specific Architectures.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a well-run Architecture Repository?
o: It captures every artifact listed in the TOGAF Standard
It minimizes the information gathered and maintained to what is needed
It is accessible only to the EA team
It cannot be used by Agile organizations
questions.e: A well-run repository minimizes information gathered and maintained; anything not needed for the current project or that adds minimal traceability should not be captured.

questions.q: What does the Gap Analysis technique primarily highlight?
o: Shortfalls between the Baseline and Target Architectures
The cost of each work package
questions.e: Gap Analysis highlights shortfalls between the Baseline and Target Architectures: items deliberately omitted, accidentally left out, or not yet defined.

questions.q: How many phases does the ADM cycle contain, excluding the Preliminary Phase and Requirements Management?
questions.e: The ADM cycle has eight phases (A through H). The Preliminary Phase precedes the cycle and Requirements Management sits in the centre, continuously.

questions.q: According to the TOGAF Standard, what does it mean when a deliverable is designated 'approved'?
o: It is finalized and cannot change
It has been reviewed and approved, but is not necessarily finalized
It has been archived in the repository
questions.e: Approved means reviewed and approved per governance practices; it does not mean finalized. Approved documents may evolve in later phases through change control.

questions.q: Which statement about the ADM cycle is correct?
o: It is a linear waterfall process that must be followed in strict sequence
It is an iterative method and the graphic shows essential information flows, not a mandated sequence
Phases may never be revisited once completed
It mandates that all four domains be completed before Phase E
questions.e: The ADM is iterative; the graphic is a stylized representation of essential information flows, not a mandated activity sequence or waterfall.

questions.q: Which of the following is an objective of the Preliminary Phase?
o: To establish the Architecture Capability including the governance process
To finalize the Implementation and Migration Plan
To obtain approval for the Statement of Architecture Work
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase establishes the Architecture Capability, tailors the framework, defines principles, and establishes (not operates) the Architecture Governance process.

questions.q: Which deliverable is created and approved in Phase A and defines the scope and approach for the architecture cycle?
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work is developed and approved in Phase A; it defines the scope and approach and is the document against which execution is measured.

questions.q: Which two architecture domains are developed in Phase C?
questions.e: Phase C covers the Information Systems Architectures: Data Architecture and Application Architecture.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of Phase E, Opportunities and Solutions?
o: To perform initial implementation planning and identify delivery vehicles
questions.e: Phase E performs initial implementation planning, identifies delivery vehicles (programs, projects, portfolios), and determines Transition Architectures.

questions.q: What is finalized in Phase F, Migration Planning?
o: The detailed Implementation and Migration Plan
questions.e: Phase F finalizes the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and confirms the Architecture Roadmap; the ADD and Architecture Requirements Specification are also finalized here.

questions.q: In which ADM phase does the TOGAF Standard align with Agile development?
questions.e: TOGAF aligns with Agile development in Phase G, Implementation Governance.

questions.q: Phase H, Architecture Change Management, is best described as which of the following?
o: The phase that develops the Target Architecture
A holding phase that keeps the ADM running and decides update vs. new cycle
The phase that creates the Architecture Vision
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase that keeps the ADM running; a Change Request may trigger a light update or a full new ADM cycle.

questions.q: Where does Requirements Management sit in the ADM, and how often does it operate?
o: Between Phase A and B, once per cycle
At the centre of the ADM, continuously across all phases
After Phase H, at the end of the cycle
questions.e: Requirements Management sits at the centre of the ADM and operates continuously, managing requirements across all phases through governance.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a purpose of Architecture Principles?
o: To form a contract between the sponsor and the Enterprise Architect
To set precedence during trade-off discussions and enable decision-making
To describe the impacts of deploying the Target Architecture
questions.e: Principles enable decision-making by setting precedence during trade-off discussions, aligning the enterprise, supporting governance, and reflecting values and culture.

questions.q: Which section of the TOGAF template for Architecture Principles states the requirements for Business and IT to carry out the principle?
questions.e: The template is Name / Statement / Rationale / Implications. Implications highlight the requirements for Business and IT to carry out the principle.

questions.q: A set of Architecture Principles that are enduring yet able to accommodate change meets which recommended criterion?
questions.e: Enduring yet able to accommodate change corresponds to the Stability criterion. The five criteria are Understandable, Robust, Complete, Consistent, and Stable.

questions.q: What is a business scenario primarily used to do?
o: Identify and understand business needs and derive requirements
Assign business value to work packages
questions.e: Business scenarios help identify and understand business needs and derive the architecture requirements the architecture must address, primarily in Phases A and B.

questions.q: What does the Business Transformation Readiness Assessment technique evaluate?
o: The technical feasibility of a solution
The organization's readiness to undergo change
questions.e: The BTRA evaluates and quantifies an organization's readiness to undergo change, applied in Phase A with mitigations feeding the Implementation and Migration Plan.

questions.q: What are the two levels of risk considered in TOGAF risk management?
questions.e: Initial Level of Risk is categorization before mitigation; Residual Level of Risk is categorization after mitigating actions are applied.

questions.q: Why is iteration important when applying the ADM?
o: It supports projects operating multiple ADM phases concurrently
questions.e: Iteration within an ADM cycle supports projects that operate multiple ADM phases concurrently.

questions.q: What are the three levels of the Architecture Landscape?
questions.e: The Architecture Landscape has three levels: Strategic, Segment, and Capability Architectures. Baseline/Transition/Target are states, not levels.

questions.q: Which statement about architecture partitioning is correct?
o: TOGAF mandates a single partitioning model
Each enterprise adopts a partitioning model that reflects its own operating model
Partitioning is required only for Agile enterprises
Partitioning must mirror the organizational chart
questions.e: It is impractical to define one partitioning model; each enterprise adopts a model reflecting its own operating model.

questions.q: Which scope dimension considers the appropriate level of detail to capture based on the intended use of the architecture?
questions.e: The four dimensions are Breadth, Depth, Time Period, and Architecture Domain. Depth addresses the appropriate level of detail for the intended use.

questions.q: How does Architecture Governance typically operate?
o: At the top level of the organization only
Within a hierarchy of governance structures
Solely within Phase G of the ADM
questions.e: Architecture Governance operates within a hierarchy that can include Corporate, Technology, IT, and Architecture Governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the Architecture Board?
o: Allocating budget for all IT projects
Writing the code for implementation projects
questions.e: Enforcement of architecture compliance is a core Architecture Board responsibility, along with providing the basis for decisions and consistency of the architecture.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: Architecture Contracts should …
o: permit deviations from principles and standards
include agreements with all parties involved in delivery of the architecture
only involve the sponsor and the architecture function
be created in the Preliminary Phase
questions.e: Because more delivery is done by integrators and providers, Architecture Contracts should establish joint agreements between all parties involved in development and delivery.

questions.q: Which pair of roles does the architect perform during an Architecture Compliance Review?
questions.e: During a compliance review the architect acts as auditor (assessing compliance) and advisor (recommending actions). Recommendations are to enforce compliance, grant a dispensation, or change the target architecture.

questions.q: What is the relationship between an architecture view and an architecture viewpoint?
o: A view is generic and reusable; a viewpoint is specific
A viewpoint governs the construction of a view; the view is specific to the architecture
They are synonyms in the TOGAF Standard
A viewpoint is always a diagram; a view is always a matrix
questions.e: A viewpoint is the generic, reusable lens defining conventions; a view is the specific representation built from a viewpoint for a set of concerns.

questions.q: In the TOGAF Standard, what is the relationship between concerns and requirements?
questions.e: Concerns are interests in a system relevant to stakeholders; identifying concerns ensures stakeholder interests become requirements.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes an Architecture Building Block (ABB) from a Solution Building Block (SBB)?
o: An ABB is implementation-specific; an SBB is logical
An ABB is logical and supplier-independent; an SBB is physical and implementation-specific
questions.e: An ABB is a logical, supplier-independent capability description that shapes the SBB; an SBB is the physical, implementation-specific component that delivers the solution.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Architecture Definition Document (ADD)?
o: To provide a high-level aspirational view of the end product
To act as a deliverable container for the core architectural artifacts
To trigger the start of an architecture development cycle
To communicate information to stakeholders at the right time
questions.e: The ADD is the deliverable container for core architectural artifacts. The aspirational view is the Architecture Vision; the trigger is the Request for Architecture Work; the communication is the Communications Plan.

questions.q: Which deliverable is sent from the sponsoring organization to trigger the start of an architecture development cycle?
questions.e: The Request for Architecture Work is sent from the sponsoring organization to the architecture organization to trigger a cycle; it is a primary output of the Preliminary Phase.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Architecture Roadmap?
o: To show progression of change from the Baseline to the Target Architecture
To act as the deliverable container for artifacts
To assess the organization's readiness for change
To define the scope and approach of the cycle
questions.e: The Architecture Roadmap lists work packages on a timeline to show progression from the Baseline to the Target Architecture. It is first produced in Phase E.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of a Change Request?
o: To communicate architecture information to stakeholders
To distribute compliance results to the Architecture Board
To request a dispensation or kick-start a further cycle of architecture work
To review project progress against objectives
questions.e: A Change Request requests a dispensation or kick-starts a further cycle of architecture work; it is the key input to Phase H.

questions.q: How is the TOGAF Content Framework structured?
o: In line with the phases of the ADM
questions.e: The Content Framework is structured in line with the phases of the ADM, providing a model for the artifacts and deliverables created in each phase.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an Architecture Capability?
o: The technology stack used to store artifacts
The organization structures, roles, responsibilities, skills, and processes to do EA
questions.e: An Architecture Capability is the ability to perform EA, put in place through organization structures, roles, responsibilities, skills, and processes; it is established in the Preliminary Phase.
